Name: Rule30Research
Description: Research provenance and dependency-aware assessments. Human-readable proofs remain imported assertions, not formal certificates.

Assertions.Description: Every claim in the ledger: definitions, theorems, finite verifications, hypotheses and falsified attempts.

schema.name: AssertionId
schema.Description: AssertionId

schema.name: Name
schema.Description: Name

schema.name: Statement
schema.Description: Statement

schema.name: ReportedStatus
schema.Description: ReportedStatus

schema.name: ProofSection
schema.Description: ProofSection

schema.name: Kind
schema.Description: Role of the claim in the research: Definition, Theorem, Known result, Finite check, Hypothesis, Bridge obligation or Prize problem.

schema.name: IntroducedInLoop
schema.Description: The Effortless loop that added this claim; empty for claims carried over from research v05.

schema.name: StatusGroup
schema.Description: Proved (definition, proved, rederived known or Lean-verified), Checked (finite verification only), Falsified, Superseded or Open.

schema.name: PremiseCount
schema.Description: Direct premises this claim depends on.

schema.name: DependentCount
schema.Description: Claims that list this one as a direct premise.

schema.name: EvidenceCount
schema.Description: Evidence files linked to this claim.

schema.name: RevisionCount
schema.Description: Recorded status changes of this claim.

schema.name: IsUsable
schema.Description: 1 when the claim may be used as a premise.

schema.name: IsProofEligible
schema.Description: 1 when the claim may be used in a proof (finite checks may not).

schema.name: DescendantCount
schema.Description: Claims that rest on this one, directly or transitively.

schema.name: Predicate
schema.Description: The modeled predicate this claim is about, if any.

schema.name: PredicateVerdict
schema.Description: The model's verdict on the predicate's bounded instances.

schema.name: PredicateIsFinitelyDecidable
schema.Description: 1 when the model can decide the full statement.

schema.name: IsModelLinked
schema.Description: 1 when the claim is tied to a modeled predicate.

schema.name: PredicateIsRefuted
schema.Description: 1 when a counterexample instance fails in the model.

schema.name: PredicateIsVerified
schema.Description: 1 when the model decides the statement true.

schema.name: EffectiveStatus
schema.Description: The status the ledger uses: FALSIFIED when the model holds a counterexample; LEAN_VERIFIED when the Lean kernel accepts a proof of the claim (or confirms a kit result); OPEN for a reported Lean result the check here does not confirm; FINITE_VERIFIED when the model decides an open or checked claim true; otherwise the reported status.

schema.name: IsModelDecided
schema.Description: 1 when the model, not a report, decides the status.

schema.name: IsModelContradicted
schema.Description: 1 when the report asserts the claim (proved, Lean-verified, checked or definitional) and the model refutes it: the report is wrong. An OPEN claim the model refutes is decided, not contradicted.

schema.name: ModelVerdict
schema.Description: The model's verdict on the claim's predicate; NOT MODELED for a claim stated only in words.

schema.name: IsCached
schema.Description: 1 when the *Cache fields of this row hold the last fresh compile (filled by loop_tools.build, cleared by every save).

schema.name: IsModelLinkedCache
schema.Description: Cached IsModelLinked from the last fresh compile; read by IsModelLinked while IsCached = 1.

schema.name: ModelVerdictCache
schema.Description: Cached ModelVerdict from the last fresh compile; read by ModelVerdict while IsCached = 1.

schema.name: EffectiveStatusCache
schema.Description: Cached EffectiveStatus from the last fresh compile; read by EffectiveStatus while IsCached = 1.

schema.name: IsModelDecidedCache
schema.Description: Cached IsModelDecided from the last fresh compile; read by IsModelDecided while IsCached = 1.

schema.name: IsModelContradictedCache
schema.Description: Cached IsModelContradicted from the last fresh compile; read by IsModelContradicted while IsCached = 1.

schema.name: StatusGroupCache
schema.Description: Cached StatusGroup from the last fresh compile; read by StatusGroup while IsCached = 1.

schema.name: IsUsableCache
schema.Description: Cached IsUsable from the last fresh compile; read by IsUsable while IsCached = 1.

schema.name: IsProofEligibleCache
schema.Description: Cached IsProofEligible from the last fresh compile; read by IsProofEligible while IsCached = 1.

schema.name: Source
schema.Description: Where a claim comes from: kit for the kit's results; empty for this ledger's own claims.

schema.name: LeanModule
schema.Description: For a kit result: its module.

schema.name: LeanDeclaration
schema.Description: The Lean declaration that states the claim: a prize problem's official statement, a kit case's headline theorem.

schema.name: LeanStatement
schema.Description: The claim's statement in Lean, written by the build from its term tree (empty while some operator has no Lean meaning).

schema.name: IsLeanExpressible
schema.Description: 1 when the build writes the statement in Lean.

schema.name: LeanCheckCount
schema.Description: Kernel checks of the current Lean statement.

schema.name: LeanCheckOk
schema.Description: Kernel checks of the current Lean statement that passed.

schema.name: IsOfficiallyAligned
schema.Description: 1 when Lean proves the claim's statement equivalent to the official one.

schema.name: IsKitModuleLinked
schema.Description: 1 when the claim is a kit module.

schema.name: IsKitDeclarationLinked
schema.Description: 1 when a Lean declaration states the claim.

schema.name: LeanModuleIsVerified
schema.Description: 1 when the kit module is verified.

schema.name: LeanDeclarationIsVerified
schema.Description: 1 when the Lean declaration is a verified theorem.

schema.name: LeanModuleUrl
schema.Description: The kit module's file.

schema.name: IsOwnClaim
schema.Description: 1 for this ledger's own claims, 0 for the kit's.

schema.name: IsLeanLinked
schema.Description: 1 when the claim has a Lean form: its own Lean statement, a kit module or a Lean declaration.

schema.name: IsFormallyStated
schema.Description: 1 when the claim is stated formally: as a term tree of the model or in Lean.

schema.name: IsLeanVerified
schema.Description: 1 when the kernel accepted a proof of the claim's current Lean statement here, or the claim is a kit result reported proved and its module (or theorem) is verified here.

schema.name: KitLinkCount
schema.Description: Kit declarations linked to this claim.

schema.name: KitCoverCount
schema.Description: Verified kit theorems that state this claim or more.

schema.name: KitContradictionCount
schema.Description: Verified kit theorems that refute this claim. Must be 0 for a claim we hold.

schema.name: KitJointCount
schema.Description: Kit theorems whose conjunction is this claim.

schema.name: KitJointVerifiedCount
schema.Description: Of those, the verified ones.

schema.name: KitGlueProofCount
schema.Description: Lean proofs of this claim that only restate kit theorems.

schema.name: IsKnownInKit
schema.Description: 1 when the kit already proves this claim (a verified kit theorem says it or more, the jointly linked ones are all verified, or its Lean proof only restates the kit): not new against the catalog.

schema.name: IsKitContradicted
schema.Description: 1 when a verified kit theorem refutes a claim the ledger holds (usable). A falsified claim the kit also refutes is agreement, not contradiction.

schema.name: IsLeanContradicted
schema.Description: 1 when Lean proves a claim the model or the ledger refutes. Must be 0.

schema.name: IsLeanUnconfirmed
schema.Description: 1 when a source reports the claim proved in Lean and the check here does not confirm it. Must be 0.

schema.name: ProofBasis
schema.Description: What the status rests on: the Lean kernel, the model, or a report.

schema.name: OnCurrentPath
schema.Description: 1 when the claim is a step of the plan in force.

schema.name: LoopTargetCount
schema.Description: Loops (planned, running or done) linked to this claim.

schema.name: LeanDeclarationUrl
schema.Description: Where the Lean declaration is: read its statement there.

data.Statement: Single seed, infinite lattice, Rule 30, time starts at zero.
data.Name: D0

data.Statement: Cone support and both boundary cells equal one.
data.Name: T0

data.Statement: Fixed diagonal k has period dividing 2^k.
data.Name: T004

data.Statement: Least antiderivative period is Q or 2Q according to forcing parity.
data.Name: TA

data.Statement: First diagonal one occurs at ceil(k/2); least period exceeds that time.
data.Name: TB

data.Statement: For every T,p a mismatch occurs in column 0 or 1 by t=2T+p.
data.Name: TC

data.Statement: Constant center runs obey the proved endpoint bounds.
data.Name: TD

data.Statement: The center is not eventually constant.
data.Name: K1

data.Statement: Generic n-step output is XOR-affine in its extreme-left input.
data.Name: TE

data.Statement: Time-indexed CMCC equations uniquely reproduce Rule 30.
data.Name: CM

data.Statement: All supplied numerical outputs reproduced.
data.Name: F1

data.Statement: Exact diagonal periods certified through offset 51.
data.Name: F2

data.Statement: 100001 center bits checked twice; periods 1..10000 excluded for onsets through 90000.
data.Name: F3

data.Statement: 33411 SQLite cells match independent evolution.
data.Name: F4

data.Statement: All diagonals k>=1 are balanced over their least period.
data.Name: H1

data.Statement: Periods double at every k>=3.
data.Name: H2

data.Statement: Cone support, first arrival and unbounded diagonal periods imply aperiodic moving diagonal.
data.Name: H3

data.Statement: Least diagonal periods never decrease.
data.Name: H4

data.Statement: ACID alone implies transaction-order independence.
data.Name: H5

data.Statement: Scalar aggregation results may always be nested without preserving group weights.
data.Name: H6

data.Statement: Periodic center of every p>=2 forces a contradiction with seed-compatible neighboring columns.
data.ProofSection: research/loop-22-left-consistent/PROOFS.md §B9 (B1 from B9 and TX); earlier route research/loop-13-top-down/PROOFS.md §Route L
data.Name: B1

data.Statement: Uniform sublinear center discrepancy bound.
data.Name: B2

data.Statement: Uniform machine-model lower bound with agreed asymptotic quantifiers.
data.Name: B3

data.Statement: The Rule 30 center is not eventually periodic.
data.Name: P1

data.Statement: The center has limiting frequency one-half.
data.Name: P2

data.Statement: The official computational-effort conjecture, once model and quantifiers are fixed.
data.Name: P3

data.Statement: For k>=3 and P=max(P_{k-1},P_{k-2}): if q_k(P/2)=1 then the least period of the forcing word q_k=y_{k-1} OR y_{k-2} is exactly P.
data.Name: TF

data.Statement: If j>=1 and eps_j=1 (least period of y_j is twice that of its forcing word) then y_j(P_j/2)=1.
data.Name: TG

data.Statement: For k>=3, if some parent j in {k-1,k-2} attains P=max(P_{k-1},P_{k-2}) and has eps_j=1, then Q_k=P.
data.Name: TH

data.Statement: For all k>=3 the least period of the forcing word equals max(P_{k-1},P_{k-2}); no OR of two parent diagonals ever has a period smaller than both.
data.Name: H7

data.Statement: If H7 holds for all k>=3 then the least diagonal periods are nondecreasing (H7 implies H4).
data.Name: TI

data.Statement: Exact least diagonal periods, forcing periods and parities certified through offset 64 (largest period 2^27) by an independent big-integer implementation that reproduces all 52 v05 period-word hashes and agrees with a direct lattice evolution for t<=4096.
data.Name: F5

data.Statement: Every diagonal is 1 at its half period: y_j(P_j/2)=1 for all j>=1 (would close the open case of H7 through TF at t=0).
data.Name: H14

data.Statement: Cascade lemma: for k>=4 and P=max(P_{k-1},P_{k-2}), if y_j(P/2)=1 for some 2<=j<=k-1 then Q_k=P.
data.Name: TJ

data.Statement: For every k>=3, Q_k=max(P_{k-1},P_{k-2}), and the least diagonal periods are nondecreasing (induction on k using TJ, TG, TA).
data.Name: TK

data.Statement: For every k>=3, P_k = P_{k-1}*(1+eps_k): the least period repeats or doubles, never otherwise; and it doubles infinitely often.
data.Name: TL

data.Statement: For k>=4, if eps_{k-1}=1 then eps_k = ones_{k-2} mod 2 (doubling at k decided by the parity of the grandparent diagonal).
data.Name: H15

data.Statement: eps_k = ones_{k-2} mod 2 for every k>=4, with no doubling assumption on k-1.
data.Name: H16

data.Statement: After a doubling at k-1 (k>=4), eps_k equals the parity of the number of ones of y_{k-2} over its least period.
data.Name: TM

data.Statement: For k>=5 the least diagonal period never doubles three times in a row; hence log2 P_k <= log2 P_k0 + ceil(2(k-k0)/3).
data.Name: TN

data.Statement: Finite discrepancy: |2 S(N) - N| <= 3 sqrt(N) for all 16 <= N <= 2^20, S(N) the number of ones among c(0..N-1).
data.Name: H9

data.Statement: Finite run bound: every maximal constant center run [T,V] with 1 <= T and V < 2^20 - 1 has length <= 2 log2(T+1) + 4.
data.Name: H13

data.Statement: For every period 1 <= p <= 2^17 and every onset T <= 917498, some t >= T has c(t) != c(t+p) (2^20 center bits; independent reproduction of E2).
data.Name: F6

data.Statement: Every plateau of the doubling sequence (maximal run of eps_k=0, k>=3) has length at most 7.
data.Name: H18

data.Statement: If every plateau has length at most L, then log2 P_k >= 2 + floor((k-3)/(L+1)) for all k>=3; a plateau bound forces exponential growth of the diagonal periods.
data.Name: TP

data.Statement: Exact diagonal periods certified through offset 72 (largest period 2^31); all 64 E10 period-word hashes reproduced; new diagonals agree with a direct lattice for t<=4096.
data.Name: F7

data.Statement: For k>=3: if eps_k=1 the diagonal has an even number of ones per period; if eps_k=0 that parity equals the parity of the number of ones of q_k at odd positions.
data.Name: TO

data.Statement: eps_k is a function of (eps_{k-1}, eps_{k-2}, o_{k-1}, o_{k-2}) for every k>=5, where o_j is the parity of the number of ones of y_j per period.
data.Name: H19

data.Statement: The center is eventually p-periodic iff some agreement run c(t)=c(t+p) is infinite; so a finite bound on agreement runs for every p implies P1.
data.Name: TQ

data.Statement: On the first 2^20 center bits, every agreement run c(t)=c(t+p) for 1<=p<=4096 has length at most 44.
data.Name: H21

data.Statement: Every left-edge diagonal w_k(t)=x(-t+k,t) is eventually periodic, with least eventual period a power of two dividing 2^k.
data.Name: TR

data.Statement: Exact least eventual periods and onsets of the left-edge diagonals certified for k<=72 (largest period 2^3, latest onset 100); agrees with a direct lattice for t<=4096.
data.Name: F8

data.Statement: The left edge grows at most half as fast as the right: log2(left-edge period of w_k) <= log2(P_k)/2 for every k>=1.
data.Name: H22

data.Statement: Every left-edge diagonal w_k has least eventual period at most 8.
data.Name: H23

data.Statement: Exact left-edge periods and onsets certified for k<=600; reproduces loop 9 for k<=72 and a direct lattice for t<=1600.
data.Name: F9

data.Statement: The left-edge front moves at 5/4: |onset_k/k - 5/4| <= 0.02 for every 1000 <= k <= 5000.
data.Name: H24

data.Statement: Exact left-edge periods and onsets certified for k<=5000; reproduces loop 10 for k<=600 and a direct lattice for t<=1600.
data.Name: F10

data.Statement: Some left-edge diagonal with k < 20000 has least eventual period 32.
data.Name: H25

data.Statement: Exact left-edge periods and onsets certified for k<=19999; for every 20<=k<=19999 the onset exceeds k, so the center c(t)=w_t(t) is read before its left-edge diagonal settles.
data.Name: F11

data.Statement: If the center p-agrees at t and t+1 then column -1 p-agrees at t when c(t)=1, and column -1 p-agrees at t iff column 1 does when c(t)=0: under center agreement, column -1 is column 1 read at the center's zero-times.
data.Name: TS

data.Statement: For every onset 1<=T<=10 and every nonconstant primitive word a of period p<=4, the left cone and the inverse rule alone exclude a p-periodic center of word a from onset T: no column-1 window is compatible once L reaches some L<=4T+4p+8.
data.Name: H26

data.Statement: Left-cone relaxation table for every onset T<=10 and every primitive word of period <=4: the number of column-1 windows (on the zero-times) compatible with a periodic center and the single-seed cone, for L<=4T+4p+8, with the first L that has none; the true (c,r) windows pass the same checker.
data.Name: F12

data.Statement: For every onset T, every p>=2 and every nonconstant word a of least period p, the left-cone relaxation (periodic center word a from T, free column 1, inverse rule, cone of T0) is unsatisfiable at some finite L(T,a).
data.Name: B5

data.Statement: For L>=T the left-cone relaxation is in bijection with rows R at time T on positions -T+1..-1 such that the Rule 30 evolution of the left half from R, with the center prescribed as boundary x(0,t)=c'(t), satisfies x(-1,t)=NOT c'(t+1) at every one-time t<=T+L-1; column 1 is determined, and count(T,a,L)<=2^(T-1).
data.Name: TU

data.Statement: For every primitive nonconstant word a of period p<=6 and every onset 2<=T<=T_max(a) that exact enumeration completes (live-set cap 2^23), the left cone excludes the periodic center with L(T,a)<=4T+4p+8.
data.Name: H27

data.Statement: Exclusion lengths L(T,a) of the left-cone relaxation for every primitive word of period <=6, onsets from 2 up to the enumeration limit per word (largest completed onset 144); vectorised search validated against the loop 13 table and an independent SAT encoding of TU.
data.Name: F13

data.Statement: For t>=T and j<=t-T, x(-1,t) = x(-j-1,t-j) XOR XOR_{i=1..j}(x(-i,t-i) OR x(-i+1,t-i)); in the relaxation the leading term is a free row bit for t<=2T-2, the edge for t=2T-1 and 0 for t>=2T, so every one-time constraint from time 2T on is a parity of ORs along a light ray with no free-row term.
data.Name: TV

data.Statement: For every primitive nonconstant word of period 7 or 8 and every onset T>=8 that exact enumeration completes (cap 2^23), the left-cone exclusion excess L(T,a)-T is at most 64: the relaxation dies by time 2T+64, independently of T.
data.Name: H28

data.Statement: Exclusion lengths, death times and violated cone cells of the left-cone relaxation for all 366 primitive words of periods 7 and 8 at onsets [8, 16, 24, 32, 48, 64, 96, 128, 160, 192] up to the enumeration limit (largest completed 192); death-cell histograms recorded.
data.Name: F14

data.Statement: For the single-zero words a=0 1^(p-1), p in [8, 10, 12, 16], and every onset T>=32 that exact enumeration completes (cap 2^25), the left-cone exclusion excess L(T,a)-T is at most 64.
data.Name: H29

data.Statement: Exclusion lengths, excess and death cells of the left-cone relaxation for the single-zero words of periods [8, 10, 12, 16] at onsets from 32 to the enumeration limit (largest completed 384), with the excess fitted against T and log2 T.
data.Name: F15

data.Statement: In the forward form, the one-time constraints at T<=t<=2T-2 fix the row bit at position -(t-T+1) as a function of the bits to its right and leave the bits at zero-time positions free: exactly 2^Z rows survive to 2T-2 (Z = zero-times in [T,2T-2]), and every constraint at t>=2T-1 is a Boolean function of those Z bits.
data.Name: TW

data.Statement: For every T>=2 and every nonconstant periodic word, each of the 2^Z rows of TW violates x(-1,t)=NOT c'(t+1) at some one-time t>=2T-1.
data.Name: B6

data.Statement: For every nonconstant primitive word of period p<=5 and every onset 4<=T<=18, the largest algebraic degree over the Z free bits among the one-time constraints applied before death is at least Z-1: the kill is maximally nonlinear, so B6 is not linear algebra over GF(2).
data.Name: H30

data.Statement: For every nonconstant primitive word of period <=5 and onset 4..18: Z, the TW count check, and for each one-time constraint after 2T-2 until death its algebraic degree over the Z free bits, live counts before and after, and whether it was constant on the live set.
data.Name: F16

data.Statement: For the words 01 and 10 and every onset 4<=T<=46, a cone cell violated by every surviving window exists at the death step, and its time t*(T) is non-decreasing in T with steps 0 or 1.
data.Name: H31

data.Statement: For the words 01 and 10 at onsets 4..46: the death window, survivors, the violated cone cells with counts, the common killing cells, whether the edge cell is among them, and t*(T).
data.Name: F17

data.Statement: B6 for the period-2 words 01 and 10: for every onset T>=2, each TW row for a 2-periodic center violates a one-time constraint at or after 2T-1 (equivalently, the Rule 30 center is not eventually 2-periodic).
data.Name: B7

data.Statement: B6 for every nonconstant word of least period p>=3.
data.Name: B8

data.Statement: The dyadic wall is exact for period 2 past onset 36: for a=01 and every onset 47<=T<=50 the left-cone relaxation dies at window exactly 64, and for a=10 at exactly 65.
data.Name: H32

data.Statement: L(T) for the words 01 and 10 at every onset 2<=T<=50 (loop 18 data plus onsets 2, 3 and 47..50 computed here with cap 2^26), with survivors at the death step.
data.Name: F18

data.Statement: The 64-wall is exactly the TW boundary phenomenon: for the words 011,101,110 (pinned window 66) and 0111,1011,1101,1110 (pinned window 64) the death window keeps its pinned value from the first pinned onset through T=63 and exceeds it at T=64,65,66; for 01 and 10 at onsets 51 and 52 it stays at 64 and 65.
data.Name: H33

data.Statement: Structure of the 64-wall for the word 01 at onsets 37..46: forced cells on the death ray (none in the cone interior), tie classes by column (columns 1-3 tied, 4-5 partly, 6 onward untied), GF(2) independence of the 33 one-time functions over all rows for T<=18; and the L(T) table of H33 for period-3 and period-4 words at onsets 44..66.
data.Name: F19

data.Statement: With every settled left-edge diagonal imposed on the periodic-center relaxation (exact values, or periodicity only), the death window exceeds the settled frontier by at most 8 (exact) or 16 (periodic only) for the words 01 and 10 at every onset 8<=T<=160 the search completes: the clash with the settled zone is local.
data.Name: H34

data.Statement: Settled-zone relaxation table for the words 01 and 10, exact and periodicity-only modes, onsets 8..160: frontier, death window, excess, peak live set, failing columns; the true lattice satisfies every imposed constraint to time 400.
data.Name: F20

data.Statement: The left half x(i,t), i<=-1, is a function of c(0..t-1) and the seed, and whenever c(t)=1 the forward rule forces c(t+1)=NOT x(-1,t): the center is left-consistent.
data.Name: TX

data.Statement: No left-consistent sequence (c(0)=1, and c(t+1)=NOT x(-1,t) whenever c(t)=1, with x the left half it generates from the seed) ends in a periodic tail with a nonconstant word.
data.Name: B9

data.Statement: For the words 01 and 10 and every onset 4<=T<=46, every left-consistent prefix c(0..T-1) is killed by the 2-periodic tail before time 2T-1, inside the zone where the free-row relaxation provably cannot kill (TW).
data.Name: H35

data.Statement: For every nonconstant primitive word of period 3 or 4 and every onset 4<=T<=32, every left-consistent prefix is killed by the periodic tail before time 2T-1.
data.Name: H36

data.Statement: Seeded relaxation table: for the words 01, 10 (onsets 4..46) and every primitive word of period 3 and 4 (onsets 4..32), the number of left-consistent prefixes, survivors, and the largest and mean death excess t*-T with its histogram; tree growth ratio 1.4981 per step.
data.Name: F21

data.Statement: For some E>=12, the near-center windows (c(t), x(-1..-E,t)) shown by left-consistent sequences at t=45 miss at least half of the 2^(E+1) possible windows.
data.Name: H37

data.Statement: There is an E<=30 such that every width-(E+1) near-center window shown by a left-consistent sequence at any time 19<=t<=45 dies within E-1 steps under the tail 01 and under the tail 10 (the finite part K(E) of B9 for period 2).
data.Name: H38

data.Statement: Near-center window language of left-consistent sequences for E=4..30 (even) and t=19..45: language sizes, stability in t (E<=22), the smallest missing windows, and the windows surviving E-1 steps under each period-2 tail.
data.Name: F22

data.Statement: H39: on the real prefix, left-consistency kills every nonconstant primitive tail a with |a| <= 3, spliced on at any onset 1 <= T <= 10, within 3|a| steps of the onset.
data.Name: H39

data.Statement: Let A be the least set of width-25 near-center windows (c(t), x(-1..-24,t)) that contains every window shown by a left-consistent prefix at t=19 and is closed under one step of the left half (outer bit free, next center bit forced by TX after a 1). For each period-2 tail, every window in A fails one of the next 24 one-time checks. H40 implies B9 for period 2 at every onset.
data.Name: H40

data.Statement: For every E >= 1, the width-(E+1) window step with the outer cell free (center NOT x(-1) after a 1, free after a 0) reaches every window from every window in at most 2E+1 steps; so the closure of any nonempty window set is all 2^(E+1) windows. A free outer cell never gives an invariant, at any width.
data.Name: TY

data.Statement: For every time 19 <= t <= 160 and each tail 01, 10, every width-25 near-center window shown at t by a left-consistent prefix fails one of the next 24 one-time checks (H38 at E=24 extended from t <= 45 to t <= 160).
data.Name: H41

data.Statement: Merged left-consistent states for t = 0..160: the number of distinct rows, the distinct width-25 windows (t >= 19), the windows among the loop 25 survivors, and the longest survival of a state under each period-2 tail (up to 120 checks).
data.Name: F23

data.Statement: The official computational-effort conjecture, once model and quantifiers are fixed.

data.Name: TF
data.Statement: For k>=3 and P=max(P_{k-1},P_{k-2}): if q_k(P/2)=1 then the least period of the forcing word q_k=y_{k-1} OR y_{k-2} is exactly P.

data.Name: TG
data.Statement: If j>=1 and eps_j=1 (least period of y_j is twice that of its forcing word) then y_j(P_j/2)=1.

data.Name: TH
data.Statement: For k>=3, if some parent j in {k-1,k-2} attains P=max(P_{k-1},P_{k-2}) and has eps_j=1, then Q_k=P.

data.Name: H7
data.Statement: For all k>=3 the least period of the forcing word equals max(P_{k-1},P_{k-2}); no OR of two parent diagonals ever has a period smaller than both.

data.Name: TI
data.Statement: If H7 holds for all k>=3 then the least diagonal periods are nondecreasing (H7 implies H4).

data.Name: F5
data.Statement: Exact least diagonal periods, forcing periods and parities certified through offset 64 (largest period 2^27) by an independent big-integer implementation that reproduces all 52 v05 period-word hashes and agrees with a direct lattice evolution for t<=4096.

data.Name: H14
data.Statement: Every diagonal is 1 at its half period: y_j(P_j/2)=1 for all j>=1 (would close the open case of H7 through TF at t=0).

data.Name: TJ
data.Statement: Cascade lemma: for k>=4 and P=max(P_{k-1},P_{k-2}), if y_j(P/2)=1 for some 2<=j<=k-1 then Q_k=P.

data.Name: TK
data.Statement: For every k>=3, Q_k=max(P_{k-1},P_{k-2}), and the least diagonal periods are nondecreasing (induction on k using TJ, TG, TA).

data.Name: TL
data.Statement: For every k>=3, P_k = P_{k-1}*(1+eps_k): the least period repeats or doubles, never otherwise; and it doubles infinitely often.

data.Name: H15
data.Statement: For k>=4, if eps_{k-1}=1 then eps_k = ones_{k-2} mod 2 (doubling at k decided by the parity of the grandparent diagonal).

data.Name: H16
data.Statement: eps_k = ones_{k-2} mod 2 for every k>=4, with no doubling assumption on k-1.

data.Name: TM
data.Statement: After a doubling at k-1 (k>=4), eps_k equals the parity of the number of ones of y_{k-2} over its least period.

data.Name: TN
data.Statement: For k>=5 the least diagonal period never doubles three times in a row; hence log2 P_k <= log2 P_k0 + ceil(2(k-k0)/3).

data.Name: H9
data.Statement: Finite discrepancy: |2 S(N) - N| <= 3 sqrt(N) for all 16 <= N <= 2^20, S(N) the number of ones among c(0..N-1).

data.Name: H13
data.Statement: Finite run bound: every maximal constant center run [T,V] with 1 <= T and V < 2^20 - 1 has length <= 2 log2(T+1) + 4.

data.Name: F6
data.Statement: For every period 1 <= p <= 2^17 and every onset T <= 917498, some t >= T has c(t) != c(t+p) (2^20 center bits; independent reproduction of E2).

data.Name: H18
data.Statement: Every plateau of the doubling sequence (maximal run of eps_k=0, k>=3) has length at most 7.

data.Name: TP
data.Statement: If every plateau has length at most L, then log2 P_k >= 2 + floor((k-3)/(L+1)) for all k>=3; a plateau bound forces exponential growth of the diagonal periods.

data.Name: F7
data.Statement: Exact diagonal periods certified through offset 72 (largest period 2^31); all 64 E10 period-word hashes reproduced; new diagonals agree with a direct lattice for t<=4096.

data.Name: TO
data.Statement: For k>=3: if eps_k=1 the diagonal has an even number of ones per period; if eps_k=0 that parity equals the parity of the number of ones of q_k at odd positions.

data.Name: H19
data.Statement: eps_k is a function of (eps_{k-1}, eps_{k-2}, o_{k-1}, o_{k-2}) for every k>=5, where o_j is the parity of the number of ones of y_j per period.

data.Name: TQ
data.Statement: The center is eventually p-periodic iff some agreement run c(t)=c(t+p) is infinite; so a finite bound on agreement runs for every p implies P1.

data.Name: H21
data.Statement: On the first 2^20 center bits, every agreement run c(t)=c(t+p) for 1<=p<=4096 has length at most 44.

data.Name: TR
data.Statement: Every left-edge diagonal w_k(t)=x(-t+k,t) is eventually periodic, with least eventual period a power of two dividing 2^k.

data.Name: F8
data.Statement: Exact least eventual periods and onsets of the left-edge diagonals certified for k<=72 (largest period 2^3, latest onset 100); agrees with a direct lattice for t<=4096.

data.Name: H22
data.Statement: The left edge grows at most half as fast as the right: log2(left-edge period of w_k) <= log2(P_k)/2 for every k>=1.

data.Name: H23
data.Statement: Every left-edge diagonal w_k has least eventual period at most 8.

data.Name: F9
data.Statement: Exact left-edge periods and onsets certified for k<=600; reproduces loop 9 for k<=72 and a direct lattice for t<=1600.

data.Name: H24
data.Statement: The left-edge front moves at 5/4: |onset_k/k - 5/4| <= 0.02 for every 1000 <= k <= 5000.

data.Name: F10
data.Statement: Exact left-edge periods and onsets certified for k<=5000; reproduces loop 10 for k<=600 and a direct lattice for t<=1600.

data.Name: H25
data.Statement: Some left-edge diagonal with k < 20000 has least eventual period 32.

data.Name: F11
data.Statement: Exact left-edge periods and onsets certified for k<=19999; for every 20<=k<=19999 the onset exceeds k, so the center c(t)=w_t(t) is read before its left-edge diagonal settles.

data.Name: TS
data.Statement: If the center p-agrees at t and t+1 then column -1 p-agrees at t when c(t)=1, and column -1 p-agrees at t iff column 1 does when c(t)=0: under center agreement, column -1 is column 1 read at the center's zero-times.

data.Name: H26
data.Statement: For every onset 1<=T<=10 and every nonconstant primitive word a of period p<=4, the left cone and the inverse rule alone exclude a p-periodic center of word a from onset T: no column-1 window is compatible once L reaches some L<=4T+4p+8.

data.Name: F12
data.Statement: Left-cone relaxation table for every onset T<=10 and every primitive word of period <=4: the number of column-1 windows (on the zero-times) compatible with a periodic center and the single-seed cone, for L<=4T+4p+8, with the first L that has none; the true (c,r) windows pass the same checker.

data.Name: B5
data.Statement: For every onset T, every p>=2 and every nonconstant word a of least period p, the left-cone relaxation (periodic center word a from T, free column 1, inverse rule, cone of T0) is unsatisfiable at some finite L(T,a).

data.Name: TU
data.Statement: For L>=T the left-cone relaxation is in bijection with rows R at time T on positions -T+1..-1 such that the Rule 30 evolution of the left half from R, with the center prescribed as boundary x(0,t)=c'(t), satisfies x(-1,t)=NOT c'(t+1) at every one-time t<=T+L-1; column 1 is determined, and count(T,a,L)<=2^(T-1).

data.Name: H27
data.Statement: For every primitive nonconstant word a of period p<=6 and every onset 2<=T<=T_max(a) that exact enumeration completes (live-set cap 2^23), the left cone excludes the periodic center with L(T,a)<=4T+4p+8.

data.Name: F13
data.Statement: Exclusion lengths L(T,a) of the left-cone relaxation for every primitive word of period <=6, onsets from 2 up to the enumeration limit per word (largest completed onset 144); vectorised search validated against the loop 13 table and an independent SAT encoding of TU.

data.Name: TV
data.Statement: For t>=T and j<=t-T, x(-1,t) = x(-j-1,t-j) XOR XOR_{i=1..j}(x(-i,t-i) OR x(-i+1,t-i)); in the relaxation the leading term is a free row bit for t<=2T-2, the edge for t=2T-1 and 0 for t>=2T, so every one-time constraint from time 2T on is a parity of ORs along a light ray with no free-row term.

data.Name: H28
data.Statement: For every primitive nonconstant word of period 7 or 8 and every onset T>=8 that exact enumeration completes (cap 2^23), the left-cone exclusion excess L(T,a)-T is at most 64: the relaxation dies by time 2T+64, independently of T.

data.Name: F14
data.Statement: Exclusion lengths, death times and violated cone cells of the left-cone relaxation for all 366 primitive words of periods 7 and 8 at onsets [8, 16, 24, 32, 48, 64, 96, 128, 160, 192] up to the enumeration limit (largest completed 192); death-cell histograms recorded.

data.Name: H29
data.Statement: For the single-zero words a=0 1^(p-1), p in [8, 10, 12, 16], and every onset T>=32 that exact enumeration completes (cap 2^25), the left-cone exclusion excess L(T,a)-T is at most 64.

data.Name: F15
data.Statement: Exclusion lengths, excess and death cells of the left-cone relaxation for the single-zero words of periods [8, 10, 12, 16] at onsets from 32 to the enumeration limit (largest completed 384), with the excess fitted against T and log2 T.

data.Name: TW
data.Statement: In the forward form, the one-time constraints at T<=t<=2T-2 fix the row bit at position -(t-T+1) as a function of the bits to its right and leave the bits at zero-time positions free: exactly 2^Z rows survive to 2T-2 (Z = zero-times in [T,2T-2]), and every constraint at t>=2T-1 is a Boolean function of those Z bits.

data.Name: B6
data.Statement: For every T>=2 and every nonconstant periodic word, each of the 2^Z rows of TW violates x(-1,t)=NOT c'(t+1) at some one-time t>=2T-1.

data.Name: H30
data.Statement: For every nonconstant primitive word of period p<=5 and every onset 4<=T<=18, the largest algebraic degree over the Z free bits among the one-time constraints applied before death is at least Z-1: the kill is maximally nonlinear, so B6 is not linear algebra over GF(2).

data.Name: F16
data.Statement: For every nonconstant primitive word of period <=5 and onset 4..18: Z, the TW count check, and for each one-time constraint after 2T-2 until death its algebraic degree over the Z free bits, live counts before and after, and whether it was constant on the live set.

data.Name: H31
data.Statement: For the words 01 and 10 and every onset 4<=T<=46, a cone cell violated by every surviving window exists at the death step, and its time t*(T) is non-decreasing in T with steps 0 or 1.

data.Name: F17
data.Statement: For the words 01 and 10 at onsets 4..46: the death window, survivors, the violated cone cells with counts, the common killing cells, whether the edge cell is among them, and t*(T).

data.Name: B7
data.Statement: B6 for the period-2 words 01 and 10: for every onset T>=2, each TW row for a 2-periodic center violates a one-time constraint at or after 2T-1 (equivalently, the Rule 30 center is not eventually 2-periodic).

data.Name: B8
data.Statement: B6 for every nonconstant word of least period p>=3.

data.Name: H32
data.Statement: The dyadic wall is exact for period 2 past onset 36: for a=01 and every onset 47<=T<=50 the left-cone relaxation dies at window exactly 64, and for a=10 at exactly 65.

data.Name: F18
data.Statement: L(T) for the words 01 and 10 at every onset 2<=T<=50 (loop 18 data plus onsets 2, 3 and 47..50 computed here with cap 2^26), with survivors at the death step.

data.Name: H33
data.Statement: The 64-wall is exactly the TW boundary phenomenon: for the words 011,101,110 (pinned window 66) and 0111,1011,1101,1110 (pinned window 64) the death window keeps its pinned value from the first pinned onset through T=63 and exceeds it at T=64,65,66; for 01 and 10 at onsets 51 and 52 it stays at 64 and 65.

data.Name: F19
data.Statement: Structure of the 64-wall for the word 01 at onsets 37..46: forced cells on the death ray (none in the cone interior), tie classes by column (columns 1-3 tied, 4-5 partly, 6 onward untied), GF(2) independence of the 33 one-time functions over all rows for T<=18; and the L(T) table of H33 for period-3 and period-4 words at onsets 44..66.

data.Name: H34
data.Statement: With every settled left-edge diagonal imposed on the periodic-center relaxation (exact values, or periodicity only), the death window exceeds the settled frontier by at most 8 (exact) or 16 (periodic only) for the words 01 and 10 at every onset 8<=T<=160 the search completes: the clash with the settled zone is local.

data.Name: F20
data.Statement: Settled-zone relaxation table for the words 01 and 10, exact and periodicity-only modes, onsets 8..160: frontier, death window, excess, peak live set, failing columns; the true lattice satisfies every imposed constraint to time 400.

data.Name: TX
data.Statement: The left half x(i,t), i<=-1, is a function of c(0..t-1) and the seed, and whenever c(t)=1 the forward rule forces c(t+1)=NOT x(-1,t): the center is left-consistent.

data.Name: B9
data.Statement: No left-consistent sequence (c(0)=1, and c(t+1)=NOT x(-1,t) whenever c(t)=1, with x the left half it generates from the seed) ends in a periodic tail with a nonconstant word.

data.Name: H35
data.Statement: For the words 01 and 10 and every onset 4<=T<=46, every left-consistent prefix c(0..T-1) is killed by the 2-periodic tail before time 2T-1, inside the zone where the free-row relaxation provably cannot kill (TW).

data.Name: H36
data.Statement: For every nonconstant primitive word of period 3 or 4 and every onset 4<=T<=32, every left-consistent prefix is killed by the periodic tail before time 2T-1.

data.Name: F21
data.Statement: Seeded relaxation table: for the words 01, 10 (onsets 4..46) and every primitive word of period 3 and 4 (onsets 4..32), the number of left-consistent prefixes, survivors, and the largest and mean death excess t*-T with its histogram; tree growth ratio 1.4981 per step.

data.Name: H37
data.Statement: For some E>=12, the near-center windows (c(t), x(-1..-E,t)) shown by left-consistent sequences at t=45 miss at least half of the 2^(E+1) possible windows.

data.Name: H38
data.Statement: There is an E<=30 such that every width-(E+1) near-center window shown by a left-consistent sequence at any time 19<=t<=45 dies within E-1 steps under the tail 01 and under the tail 10 (the finite part K(E) of B9 for period 2).

data.Name: F22
data.Statement: Near-center window language of left-consistent sequences for E=4..30 (even) and t=19..45: language sizes, stability in t (E<=22), the smallest missing windows, and the windows surviving E-1 steps under each period-2 tail.

data.Name: H39
data.Statement: H39: on the real prefix, left-consistency kills every nonconstant primitive tail a with |a| <= 3, spliced on at any onset 1 <= T <= 10, within 3|a| steps of the onset.

data.Name: H40
data.Statement: Let A be the least set of width-25 near-center windows (c(t), x(-1..-24,t)) that contains every window shown by a left-consistent prefix at t=19 and is closed under one step of the left half (outer bit free, next center bit forced by TX after a 1). For each period-2 tail, every window in A fails one of the next 24 one-time checks. H40 implies B9 for period 2 at every onset.

data.Name: TY
data.Statement: For every E >= 1, the width-(E+1) window step with the outer cell free (center NOT x(-1) after a 1, free after a 0) reaches every window from every window in at most 2E+1 steps; so the closure of any nonempty window set is all 2^(E+1) windows. A free outer cell never gives an invariant, at any width.

data.Name: H41
data.Statement: For every time 19 <= t <= 160 and each tail 01, 10, every width-25 near-center window shown at t by a left-consistent prefix fails one of the next 24 one-time checks (H38 at E=24 extended from t <= 45 to t <= 160).

data.Name: F23
data.Statement: Merged left-consistent states for t = 0..160: the number of distinct rows, the distinct width-25 windows (t >= 19), the windows among the loop 25 survivors, and the longest survival of a state under each period-2 tail (up to 120 checks).

data.Summary: Explicit z-array with cone support and first arrivals. Falsified as an implication; recurrence coupling remains essential.

data.Name: legacy-5
data.Hypothesis: Periodic adjacent columns are compatible with the seed
data.Summary: Inverse rule plus finite cone boundary. Impossible; explicit finite mismatch window proved.

data.Name: legacy-6
data.Hypothesis: A constant center tail might survive the two-column obstruction
data.Summary: One-tail forces a fixed left neighbor; zero-tail forces monotone right neighbor. Excluded for all onsets; identified as known qualitative result.

data.Name: legacy-7
data.Hypothesis: Local periodic spacetime constraints alone refute candidate center periods
data.Summary: Exhaustive pair-word graphs for p<=8. Local periodic solutions exist; seed compatibility cannot be dropped.

data.Name: legacy-8
data.Hypothesis: Input ensemble balance proves time balance
data.Summary: Sensitivity theorem and exact truth tables. Ensemble theorem proved; transfer to the fixed orbit remains unsupported.

data.Name: legacy-9
data.Hypothesis: CMCC and ordinary evolution agree
data.Summary: SQLite lookups/formulas versus independent rows. All 33,411 cells agree; representation theorem proved.

data.Name: legacy-10
data.Hypothesis: ACID / arbitrary aggregation nesting supply additional invariants
data.Summary: Explicit serial-order and unequal-group counterexamples. General implications rejected; narrow their hypotheses.

data.Name: legacy-11
data.Hypothesis: The finite center exclusions persist at a larger horizon
data.Summary: Two implementations through t=100,000. Stronger finite certificates; no infinite-time promotion.

data.Name: legacy-12
data.Hypothesis: Period calculations survive a different implementation
data.Summary: Whole triangular-state orbit replay. See data/period_verification.json.

data.Name: legacy-13

data.Summary: All 1,966 primitive words of length <=10. Every nonconstant word admits recurrent branching; the constant-zero argument does not generalize.

data.Headline: P1 waits on two open obligations, B7 (period 2) and B8 (period 3 and up), at the bottom of a chain of proved reductions. No prize problem is closer to proved; the open obligations are sharper.
data.Approach: Go after period 2 first, through B9: no left-consistent sequence ends in a 2-periodic tail. TX makes the center left-consistent, so B9 is exactly what B1 needs, and it is weaker than B5. Finite checks are strong: every left-consistent start at onsets 20 to 46 dies within 22 steps of a period-2 tail (F21), and every near-center window of width 25 that such sequences produce at times 19 to 45 dies within 23 steps (H38).
data.Missing: A uniform description of the reachable windows that still kills. Freeing the outer cell at each step reaches every window and lets 18,432 survive (H40). Tying the outer cell to the settled left-edge zone does not help for long: the settled zone starts about 0.27 t columns out (17 at t = 64, 35 at t = 128), so column 24 is settled only until about t = 85, and the unsettled band between the window and the settled zone widens without bound.
data.NextHypothesis: Does the finite kill hold past t = 45? Merge left-consistent prefixes by their row (their future depends only on it) and test every reachable state from t = 19 to t = 160 against both period-2 tails (H41). Prove that a free outer cell floods the window closure at every width (TY), which rules out widening the window without a run.
data.Estimate: Proving P1 itself: well under 1 percent, unchanged. Proving the period-2 case on this route: lowered to about 1 in 20, because the window idea needs information from a band that widens with t. Loop 26 is designed to settle whether the route is viable at all.
data.Name: after-loop-25
data.GoalStatement: The Rule 30 center is not eventually periodic.
data.NextTargetStatement: B6 for the period-2 words 01 and 10: for every onset T>=2, each TW row for a 2-periodic center violates a one-time constraint at or after 2T-1 (equivalently, the Rule 30 center is not eventually 2-periodic).

data.Headline: P1 waits on two open obligations, B7 (period 2) and B8 (period 3 and up), at the bottom of a chain of proved reductions. Loop 26 closed the near-center window route to period 2; the attack moves to whole rows.
data.Approach: Go after period 2 first, through B9: no left-consistent sequence ends in a 2-periodic tail. TX makes the center left-consistent, so B9 is exactly what B1 needs. Prefixes with the same row have the same future, so merged by row they are few: 4.6 million states at t = 160 against an extrapolated 10^28 prefixes, and every one dies under both period-2 tails (F23). A proof needs a description of the reachable rows that is closed under the step and contains only rows that die.
data.Missing: A finite description of whole reachable rows. Near-center windows cannot be it: a free outer cell floods any window closure (TY), and the kill time of real states grows with t (46 and 47 checks by t = 111, H41), so no fixed-width window kills. The far left of a row is where the settled diagonals make it periodic, so an automaton reading the row from the left edge inward may stay small.
data.NextHypothesis: Read each reachable row from the left edge inward and build the smallest automaton accepting exactly the reachable rows at each t. If its size stops growing in t through t = 160, a regular invariant is plausible and the next step is to close it under the step and check that every row it accepts dies. If it keeps growing like the state count, no regular description exists at this level and the route through B9 needs another idea.
data.Estimate: Proving P1 itself: well under 1 percent, unchanged. Proving the period-2 case through B9: about 1 in 30, lowered because the window route closed and the kill time grows with t. Loop 27 gives a decisive reading on the whole-row route.

data.GoalStatement: The Rule 30 center is not eventually periodic.
data.NextTargetStatement: B6 for the period-2 words 01 and 10: for every onset T>=2, each TW row for a 2-periodic center violates a one-time constraint at or after 2T-1 (equivalently, the Rule 30 center is not eventually 2-periodic).

data.Headline: Measured against the official challenge: period 1 and every eventual period with P <= 4096 and T <= 8192 are proved in Lean (the kit); period 2 waits on Q01, which is open, and our left-consistency route attacks the same object from the real seed.
data.Approach: Two routes to P1 meet at one frontier, period 2. The kit's route (B10) splits P1 by the least period and reduces period 2 to Q01, a statement about the zero-boundary left half from any finite start. The kit also proves barriers: no finite abstraction, local ranking or edge-DFA ranking proves Q01, because truncated stripes survive arbitrarily long. Our route (B1, B9, TX) only ever uses the left half the real seed produces, and TX is now kernel-checked. The barrier witnesses are never real left halves (Rule30ZeroBoundaryBarriers.trunc_not_left_half), so the real left halves are where a finite description can still exist.
data.Missing: B9's period-2 case stated in Lean over the kit's driven left half (Rule30DrivenLeft.L) with the real seed's rows as starts, and a proof in Lean that it gives KC4; then a description of those rows that a proof can carry.
data.NextHypothesis: Read each left half that the real seed produces at the start of a period-2 tail from the left edge inward, and build the smallest automaton accepting exactly those rows at each t. If its size stops growing in t through t = 160, a regular invariant of real left halves is plausible, and it is outside the kit's barrier B6 (which needs arbitrary finite starts). If it grows like the state count, the regular route is closed for real left halves too.
data.Estimate: Proving P1: well under 1 percent, unchanged. Period 2 (Q01, or our B7): about 1 in 30; the kit's barriers lower it for generic finite-state arguments and leave the real-seed route as the one they do not cover. A kit contribution from this ledger soon: unlikely as it stands; the claims of ours that Lean now verifies are known (K1, T0, TX, D0, T004) or elementary (TS).

data.Note: A free outer cell floods any window closure, at every width.
data.Name: after-loop-27-17
data.Statement: For every E >= 1, the width-(E+1) window step with the outer cell free (center NOT x(-1) after a 1, free after a 0) reaches every window from every window in at most 2E+1 steps; so the closure of any nonempty window set is all 2^(E+1) windows. A free outer cell never gives an invariant, at any width.

data.Note: No fixed-width window kill: the longest survival grows with t.
data.Name: after-loop-27-18

data.Name: after-loop-27-19

schema.Description: How its effort for n is counted: cone-updates (simulate the light cone) or table-read (one read).

schema.name: StoresAnswer
schema.Description: 1 when the machine contains the sequence itself.

schema.name: IsAdmissible
schema.Description: 1 when the algorithm does not store the answer.

schema.name: ComputationCount
schema.Description: Values of n computed.

schema.name: WrongOutputCount
schema.Description: Outputs that differ from c(n). Must be 0.

schema.name: RatioAtHorizon
schema.Description: effort/n at n = depth.

schema.name: RatioAtHalfHorizon
schema.Description: effort/n at n = depth/2.

schema.name: IsRatioGrowing
schema.Description: 1 when effort/n grows between half the horizon and the horizon (no sign of O(n)).

schema.name: EffortHolds
schema.Description: Problem 3 instance: an admissible algorithm shows no sign of O(n) effort (inadmissible ones are excluded, so hold vacuously).

schema.name: IsCached
schema.Description: 1 when the *Cache fields of this row hold the last fresh compile (filled by loop_tools.build, cleared by every save).

schema.name: EffortHoldsCache
schema.Description: Cached EffortHolds from the last fresh compile; read by EffortHolds while IsCached = 1.

Computations.Description: machine[m][n] = {v, t}: one algorithm computing c(n), with its output value and effort.

schema.name: ComputationId
schema.Description: <algorithm>-n<n>.

schema.name: Name
schema.Description: Display alias.

schema.name: Algorithm
schema.Description: The algorithm m.

schema.name: TimeStep
schema.Description: The target time step n.

schema.name: EffortRule
schema.Description: How effort is counted.

schema.name: TargetIndex
schema.Description: n.

schema.name: Depth
schema.Description: The horizon.

schema.name: CenterValue
schema.Description: c(n) in the model.

schema.name: ConeUpdates
schema.Description: Cell updates to reach line n.

schema.name: OutputValue
schema.Description: v: the value the algorithm outputs (both recorded algorithms read the computed cell).

schema.name: IsCorrect
schema.Description: 1 when v = c(n).

schema.name: Effort
schema.Description: t: the effort spent.

schema.name: EffortRatio
schema.Description: effort / n.

schema.name: IsHorizon
schema.Description: 1 at n = depth.

schema.name: IsHalfHorizon
schema.Description: 1 at n = depth/2.

Variables.Description: The variables the predicates quantify over, the table whose rows are their values in the model, and whether their domain is infinite in the problem.

schema.name: VariableId
schema.Description: Name of the variable.

schema.name: Name
schema.Description: Display alias.

schema.name: Symbol
schema.Description: How the problem writes it.

schema.name: Meaning
schema.Description: What it ranges over.

schema.name: DomainTable
schema.Description: The table whose rows are its values in the model (finite there).

schema.name: IsUnboundedInProblem
schema.Description: 1 when its domain in the problem is infinite.

schema.name: BinderCount
schema.Description: Quantifiers binding it, across all predicates.

schema.name: LeanType
schema.Description: Its type in Lean (Nat, Int); empty while it has no Lean meaning (words, rows, windows).

schema.name: IsLeanTyped
schema.Description: 1 when the variable has a Lean type.

data.Meaning: Index of the term to compute
data.Name: index

data.Meaning: Left cell of a neighborhood (0 or 1)
data.Name: left-bit

data.Meaning: Center cell of a neighborhood (0 or 1)
data.Name: center-bit

data.Meaning: Right cell of a neighborhood (0 or 1)
data.Name: right-bit

data.Meaning: Last time step of a constant run
data.Name: run-end

data.Meaning: A finite word whose repetition is a tail
data.Name: word

data.Meaning: Relaxation window length (or a plateau bound)
data.Name: window-length

data.Meaning: A row of free bits at time T
data.Name: row

data.Meaning: A Boolean function (finitely many for a fixed arity)
data.Name: function

data.Meaning: An output of the supplied package
data.Name: supplied-output

data.Meaning: A cell of the supplied SQLite store
data.Name: sqlite-cell

Operators.Description: The symbols formal statements are built from: binders (quantifiers, limits), connectives, relations, arithmetic and the functions of the model (c, x, rule30, cTail, ...).

schema.name: OperatorId
schema.Description: Name of the operator.

schema.name: Name
schema.Description: Display alias.

schema.name: Symbol
schema.Description: How it is written.

schema.name: Kind
schema.Description: binder, infix, prefix, apply, atom, var or const: how a term with this operator is written out.

schema.name: Arity
schema.Description: Number of arguments (a binder has two: its condition and its body).

schema.name: IsModeled
schema.Description: 1 when the model computes this operator (a table or field gives it its value); 0 when it is only a named symbol so far.

schema.name: UseCount
schema.Description: Terms using it.

schema.name: LeanForm
schema.Description: How Terms.LeanRendered writes a term with this operator: forall, exists, notexists, infix, prefix, apply, atom, var, const. Empty while the operator has no Lean meaning.

schema.name: LeanSymbol
schema.Description: The operator in Lean: syntax, or a function of the prelude in research/lean/ledger.py.

schema.name: IsLeanDefined
schema.Description: 1 when the operator has a Lean meaning.

Terms.Description: One node of a formal statement: an operator with its argument terms, a variable, or a constant. A binder holds its bound variable, its condition (Arg1) and its body (Arg2). The text, the quantifier count and whether a quantifier ranges over an infinite domain are computed from the tree.

schema.name: TermId
schema.Description: <predicate>-<preorder index>.

schema.name: Name
schema.Description: Display alias.

schema.name: TermOperator
schema.Description: The operator (var and const for leaves).

schema.name: Variable
schema.Description: The variable of a var leaf, or the variable a binder binds.

schema.name: Constant
schema.Description: The value of a const leaf.

schema.name: BoundsVariable
schema.Description: On a binder: 1 when its condition gives the variable a finite range (as in Theorem C's t in [T, 2T + p]).

schema.name: Arg1
schema.Description: First argument (a binder: its condition).

schema.name: Arg2
schema.Description: Second argument (a binder: its body).

schema.name: Arg3
schema.Description: Third argument.

schema.name: Arg4
schema.Description: Fourth argument.

schema.name: IntroducedInLoop
schema.Description: The model-native loop that added this term; empty for the core predicates.

schema.name: PredicateKey
schema.Description: The predicate whose statement this node belongs to (a plain key, not a reference: Predicates already points at the root term).

schema.name: OpSymbol
schema.Description: How the operator is written.

schema.name: OpKind
schema.Description: How the term is written out.

schema.name: OpArity
schema.Description: Number of arguments.

schema.name: OpIsModeled
schema.Description: 1 when the model computes the operator.

schema.name: VarSymbol
schema.Description: The variable as written.

schema.name: VarUnbounded
schema.Description: 1 when the variable ranges over an infinite domain.

schema.name: Arg1Text
schema.Description: Arg1 written out.

schema.name: Arg2Text
schema.Description: Arg2 written out.

schema.name: Arg3Text
schema.Description: Arg3 written out.

schema.name: Arg4Text
schema.Description: Arg4 written out.

schema.name: Rendered
schema.Description: The term written out in Wolfram Language style, computed from the tree.

schema.name: IsUnboundedBinder
schema.Description: 1 for a quantifier over an infinite domain.

schema.name: IsBinder
schema.Description: 1 for a quantifier (or another binder).

schema.name: IsUnmodeledOperator
schema.Description: 1 when the model does not compute this operator yet.

schema.name: OpLeanForm
schema.Description: How the term is written in Lean.

schema.name: OpLeanSymbol
schema.Description: The operator in Lean.

schema.name: VarLeanType
schema.Description: The variable's Lean type.

schema.name: OpIsLean
schema.Description: 1 when the operator has a Lean meaning.

schema.name: VarIsLean
schema.Description: 1 when the variable has a Lean type.

schema.name: Arg1Lean
schema.Description: Arg1 written in Lean.

schema.name: Arg2Lean
schema.Description: Arg2 written in Lean.

schema.name: Arg3Lean
schema.Description: Arg3 written in Lean.

schema.name: Arg4Lean
schema.Description: Arg4 written in Lean.

schema.name: LeanRendered
schema.Description: The term written in Lean, computed from the tree over the prelude of research/lean/ledger.py; empty when an operator or variable has no Lean meaning yet.

schema.name: IsLeanless
schema.Description: 1 when this node has no Lean meaning yet (its operator, or the type of its variable).

Predicates.Description: The properties stated about the model: definitions, theorems, bridge obligations and the three prize problems. The formal statement is a Terms tree; its bounded instances are computed from the model; a model-native loop adds its hypotheses here as rows.

schema.name: PredicateId
schema.Description: Name of the predicate.

schema.name: Name
schema.Description: Display alias.

schema.name: Problem
schema.Description: Definition, Known result, Theorem, Bridge obligation, Hypothesis, or the prize problem it is (P1, P2, P3).

schema.name: InstanceKind
schema.Description: Which reference of PredicateInstances decides an instance.

schema.name: RootTerm
schema.Description: The formal statement.

schema.name: Statement
schema.Description: A gloss in words; the formal content is the term tree.

schema.name: InstanceMeaning
schema.Description: What one bounded instance asserts.

schema.name: FailureRefutes
schema.Description: 1 when a failing instance is a counterexample to the statement; 0 when it only means the horizon did not decide it.

schema.name: BoundSlope
schema.Description: For bound hypotheses: the bound is slope * |a| + intercept.

schema.name: BoundIntercept
schema.Description: For bound hypotheses: see BoundSlope.

schema.name: DomainMin
schema.Description: For bound hypotheses: the smallest index (N, T) the statement covers.

schema.name: CoversDomain
schema.Description: 1 when the instance rows enumerate the whole bounded domain of the statement, so holding on all of them verifies it; 0 when they are a sample (a model horizon shorter than the statement).

schema.name: IntroducedInLoop
schema.Description: The model-native loop that stated this predicate; empty for the core predicates.

schema.name: Formal
schema.Description: The formal statement, written out from its term tree.

schema.name: QuantifierCount
schema.Description: Quantifiers in the statement.

schema.name: UnboundedQuantifierCount
schema.Description: Quantifiers over an infinite domain.

schema.name: UnmodeledOperatorCount
schema.Description: Operators of the statement the model does not compute yet.

schema.name: IsComputable
schema.Description: 1 when every operator of the statement has a meaning in the model.

schema.name: IsFinitelyDecidable
schema.Description: 1 when the model can decide the full statement, not only bounded instances.

schema.name: RowCount
schema.Description: Instance rows, in or out of the domain.

schema.name: InstanceCount
schema.Description: Bounded instances in the domain of the statement.

schema.name: HoldingCount
schema.Description: Instances that hold.

schema.name: FailingCount
schema.Description: Instances that fail.

schema.name: IsRefuted
schema.Description: 1 when a counterexample instance fails: the statement is false.

schema.name: IsVerified
schema.Description: 1 when the statement is finite, its instances cover its domain and every one holds: the model decides it true.

schema.name: FiniteVerdict
schema.Description: What the model says about the bounded instances.
schema.formula: =IF({{IsCached}}=1,{{FiniteVerdictCache}},IF({{InstanceCount}}=0,"NO INSTANCES",IF({{FailingCount}}=0,"HOLDS ON EVERY INSTANCE",IF({{FailureRefutes}}=1,CONCAT("REFUTED BY ",{{FailingCount}}," OF ",{{InstanceCount}}," INSTANCES"),CONCAT({{FailingCount}}," OF ",{{InstanceCount}}," UNDECIDED AT THE HORIZON")))))

schema.name: AssertionCount
schema.Description: Ledger claims about this predicate.

schema.name: LeanlessTermCount
schema.Description: Nodes of the statement with no Lean meaning yet.

schema.name: IsLeanExpressible
schema.Description: 1 when every node of the statement has a Lean meaning, so the build writes it in Lean.

schema.name: LeanRoot
schema.Description: The root term written in Lean.

schema.name: LeanStatement
schema.Description: The statement in Lean, written by the build from the term tree; empty while some node has no Lean meaning.

schema.name: IsCached
schema.Description: 1 when the *Cache fields of this row hold the last fresh compile (filled by loop_tools.build, cleared by every save).

schema.name: QuantifierCountCache
schema.Description: Cached QuantifierCount from the last fresh compile; read by QuantifierCount while IsCached = 1.

schema.name: UnboundedQuantifierCountCache
schema.Description: Cached UnboundedQuantifierCount from the last fresh compile; read by UnboundedQuantifierCount while IsCached = 1.

data.Statement: The prize setup: a single black cell at position 0 at time 0, then Rule 30 at every cell and time.
data.InstanceMeaning: One instance per run: the run is Rule 30 from the single seed.
data.Name: pr-d0-setup

data.Statement: Rule 30's table is Wolfram's polynomial (equivalently left XOR (center OR right)).
data.InstanceMeaning: One instance per transition of rule 30.
data.Name: pr-rule30-polynomial
data.Formal: ForAll[l, True, ForAll[q, True, ForAll[r, True, (rule30[l, q, r] == Mod[(((l + q) + r) + (q * r)), 2])]]]
data.LeanRoot: (∀ l : Nat, True → (∀ q : Nat, True → (∀ r : Nat, True → ((rule30 l q r) = (Mod (((l + q) + r) + (q * r)) 2)))))
data.LeanStatement: (∀ l : Nat, True → (∀ q : Nat, True → (∀ r : Nat, True → ((rule30 l q r) = (Mod (((l + q) + r) + (q * r)) 2)))))

data.Statement: From the single seed under a quiescent rule, every cell outside the light cone is white.
data.InstanceMeaning: One instance per run: the run satisfies the conditions that make the cone exact.
data.Name: pr-light-cone

data.Statement: Problem 1: the center column is not eventually periodic.
data.InstanceMeaning: One instance per period p <= 24: every candidate (p, T) with T <= (depth - p)/2 has a witness t >= T with c(t + p) != c(t) inside the horizon (the witnesses are PeriodicityCandidates.FirstMismatchFrom).
data.Name: pr-p1-non-periodic
data.Formal: NotExists[p, (p >= 1), Exists[T, (T >= 0), ForAll[t, (t >= T), (c[(t + p)] == c[t])]]]

data.Statement: The center column is not eventually constant (the period-1 case of Problem 1).
data.InstanceMeaning: One instance: every onset T <= (depth - 1)/2 has a witness t >= T with c(t + 1) != c(t).
data.Name: pr-k1-not-constant

data.Statement: Theorem C: for every T and p, column 0 or column 1 has x(i, t) != x(i, t + p) for some t in [T, 2T + p].
data.InstanceMeaning: One instance per period p: every window (T, p) that ends inside the horizon holds (the windows are MismatchWindows rows).
data.Name: pr-tc-mismatch-window

data.Statement: Theorem D: a black center run starting at T ends by 2T+1, a white one by 4T+5.
data.InstanceMeaning: One instance per center cell: the cell lies within the bound of the run it belongs to.
data.Name: pr-td-run-bounds

data.Statement: TX: whenever c(t) = 1 the rule forces c(t + 1) = NOT x(-1, t), and the left half depends only on the center's past: the center is left-consistent.
data.InstanceMeaning: One instance per time step t < depth of the real center.
data.Name: pr-tx-left-consistent

data.Statement: B9 on the real prefix: the real center up to T followed by a a a ... (a nonconstant, primitive) is not left-consistent: some one-time t has cTail(t + 1) != NOT xTail(-1, t). B9 and TX imply it; B1 follows from it.
data.InstanceMeaning: One instance per tail candidate (word, onset): left-consistency kills it inside the horizon (onset + 12).
data.Name: pr-b9-tail-killed
data.Formal: ForAll[a, (Nonconstant[a] && (LeastPeriod[a] == Length[a])), ForAll[T, (T >= 1), Exists[t, (t >= (T - 1)), ((cTail[a, T, t] == 1) && (cTail[a, T, (t + 1)] != (1 - xTail[a, T, -1, t])))]]]

data.Statement: Problem 2: each color occurs on average equally often in the center column.
data.InstanceMeaning: One instance per tolerance epsilon: the density of the whole computed prefix is within epsilon of 1/2.
data.Name: pr-p2-equal-frequency

data.Statement: Problem 3: no admissible machine computes c(n) with effort O(n) (the displayed predicate; the prose says "at least O(n)").
data.InstanceMeaning: One instance per algorithm: an admissible algorithm's effort ratio still grows at the horizon.
data.Name: pr-p3-effort
data.Formal: NotExists[m, !StoresAnswer[m], (ForAll[n, (n >= 1), (Output[m, n] == c[n])] && (Limsup[n, (n -> Infinity), (Effort[m, n] / n)] < Infinity))]

data.Statement: T0: both boundary cells of the cone are black at every time (cone support is pr-light-cone).
data.InstanceMeaning: One instance per edge diagonal: every cone cell on it is black inside the horizon.
data.Name: pr-t0-edges

data.Statement: T004: the right diagonal y_k is periodic with a period dividing 2^k.
data.InstanceMeaning: One instance per k <= 5: 2^k is a period of the observed y_k.
data.Name: pr-t004-dyadic-period

data.Statement: TB: the first black cell of y_k is at t = ceil(k/2), and its least period exceeds that time.
data.InstanceMeaning: One instance per right diagonal whose least period the horizon certifies.
data.Name: pr-tb-first-one

data.Statement: H1: every right diagonal k >= 1 is balanced over its least period.
data.InstanceMeaning: One instance per certified right diagonal k >= 1.
data.Name: pr-h1-balanced

data.Statement: H2: the least period doubles at every k >= 3.

data.Note: The official statement: the center column is not eventually periodic.
data.Name: P1>Ruliology.CellularAutomata.Rule30Prize.Problem1

data.Note: The official statement, in integers: for every k > 0, eventually k |2 blackCount n - n| <= n.
data.Name: P2>Ruliology.CellularAutomata.Rule30Prize.Problem2

data.Note: The kit's reference model of Problem 3 (one-tape Turing machine on the binary digits of n); the prize has no official Lean statement.
data.Name: P3>Ruliology.CellularAutomata.Rule30Problem3.Problem3

data.Note: The only unconditional density fact: at least log2 n black cells among the first n.
data.Name: P2>Ruliology.CellularAutomata.Rule30CenterRuns.log_two_le_blackCount

data.Note: Period 1 of Problem 1, exactly.
data.Name: K1>Ruliology.CellularAutomata.Rule30Prize.center_not_eventually_period_one

data.Note: Every column, not only the center.
data.Name: K1>Ruliology.CellularAutomata.Rule30Prize.no_column_eventually_constant

data.Note: The kit's definition of the evolution: cell 0 p = (p = 0), cell (t+1) p = rule (cell t (p-1)) (cell t p) (cell t (p+1)).
data.Name: D0>Ruliology.CellularAutomata.Rule30Jen.cell

data.Note: The left boundary cell x(-t, t) is black.
data.Name: T0>Ruliology.CellularAutomata.Rule30Jen.cell_left_edge

data.Note: The right boundary cell x(t, t) is black (R 0 t = cell t t).
data.Name: T0>Ruliology.CellularAutomata.Rule30Diagonals.R_zero

data.Note: At i = 0: if c(t) = 1 then x(-1, t) = NOT c(t + 1).
data.Name: TX>Ruliology.CellularAutomata.Rule30MaskedJen.left_of_black

data.Note: TX's second half: the left half is the half driven by the center column (L with the center as boundary).
data.Name: TX>Ruliology.CellularAutomata.Rule30DrivenLeft.cell_eq_L

data.Note: The local step behind TS when c(t) = 1.
data.Name: TS>Ruliology.CellularAutomata.Rule30MaskedJen.left_of_black

data.Note: The local step behind TS when c(t) = 0.
data.Name: TS>Ruliology.CellularAutomata.Rule30MaskedJen.left_of_white

data.Note: Left permutivity: the cell to the left is determined by the cell below and its neighbours.
data.Name: TE>Ruliology.CellularAutomata.Rule30Jen.cell_left

data.Note: A finite-window form of Jen: a period on the center and on the or-column cannot both hold over [n - P, 2n).
data.Name: TC>Ruliology.CellularAutomata.Rule30MaskedJen.finitary_jen

data.Note: With a periodic center, every window [n, 2n) past T + P has a white time where column 1 breaks the period.
data.Name: TC>Ruliology.CellularAutomata.Rule30MaskedJen.periodic_window

data.Note: A black center run starting at a >= 1 has length at most a (ours: it ends by 2T + 1).
data.Name: TD>Ruliology.CellularAutomata.Rule30CenterRuns.black_run_le

data.Note: A white center run starting at a >= 1 has length at most a - 1 (ours: it ends by 4T + 5).
data.Name: TD>Ruliology.CellularAutomata.Rule30CenterRuns.white_run_le'

data.Note: Kernel-checked: no eventual period P <= 4096 with transient T <= 8192. F3 (by computation, not in Lean) covers p <= 10000, T <= 90000.
data.Name: F3>Ruliology.CellularAutomata.Rule30Window.no_small_eventual_period

data.Note: Kernel-checked window P <= 4096, T <= 8192. F6 (by computation, not in Lean) covers p <= 2^17, T <= 917498.
data.Name: F6>Ruliology.CellularAutomata.Rule30Window.no_small_eventual_period

data.Note: Kernel-checked: any eventual period has T + P >= 16359.
data.Name: F6>Ruliology.CellularAutomata.Rule30FactorWindow.transient_add_period_ge

data.Note: Agreement runs and the transient-plus-period bound.
data.Name: H21>Ruliology.CellularAutomata.Rule30FactorWindow.transient_add_period_ge

data.Note: y_k = R k repeats with period 2^k from time 0, so its least period divides 2^k.
data.Name: T004>Ruliology.CellularAutomata.Rule30Diagonals.R_periodic

data.Note: y_k is black at ceil(k/2) (R j ((j+1)/2) = true).
data.Name: TB>Ruliology.CellularAutomata.Rule30RightPeriods.R_half

data.Note: y_k is white before ceil(k/2) (2t < j -> R j t = false).
data.Name: TB>Ruliology.CellularAutomata.Rule30RightPeriods.R_lt

data.Note: Every period of y_k (k >= 1) exceeds ceil(k/2) - 1, i.e. (k+1)/2 < P.
data.Name: TB>Ruliology.CellularAutomata.Rule30RightPeriods.period_gt

data.Note: The least dyadic exponents never decrease: e_j <= e_{j+1} (P_k = 2^{e_k}).
data.Name: H4>Ruliology.CellularAutomata.Rule30RightPeriods.e_mono

data.Note: e_{j+1} = e_j + [R_{j+1}(2^{e_j}) = 1]: the period repeats or doubles.
data.Name: TL>Ruliology.CellularAutomata.Rule30RightPeriods.e_step

data.Note: The periods are unbounded, so the period doubles infinitely often.
data.Name: TL>Ruliology.CellularAutomata.Rule30RightPeriods.not_per_small

data.Note: The period never doubles three times in a row.
data.Name: TN>Ruliology.CellularAutomata.Rule30RightPeriods.no_three

data.Note: e_{n+3} - e_{n+2} is the parity of the black input cells over one period of the input.
data.Name: TM>Ruliology.CellularAutomata.Rule30RightPeriods.S_rule

data.Note: The doubling parity rule.
data.Name: H15>Ruliology.CellularAutomata.Rule30RightPeriods.S_rule

data.Note: After a doubling, every window of one period is exactly half black.
data.Name: TO>Ruliology.CellularAutomata.Rule30RightPeriods.half_black

data.Note: The input R_{n+1} || R_n of diagonal n+2 has least period 2^{e_{n+2}}... every period of it is a multiple of that.
data.Name: H7>Ruliology.CellularAutomata.Rule30RightPeriods.inp_least_period

data.Note: Q_k = max(P_{k-1}, P_{k-2}): the least period of the forcing word.
data.Name: TK>Ruliology.CellularAutomata.Rule30RightPeriods.inp_least_period

data.Note: And the least periods are nondecreasing.
data.Name: TK>Ruliology.CellularAutomata.Rule30RightPeriods.e_mono

data.Note: Monotonicity itself, without H7.
data.Name: TI>Ruliology.CellularAutomata.Rule30RightPeriods.e_mono

data.Note: The forcing word and its least period.
data.Name: TF>Ruliology.CellularAutomata.Rule30RightPeriods.inp_least_period

data.Note: A black cell at the period makes the next diagonal antiperiodic.
data.Name: TG>Ruliology.CellularAutomata.Rule30RightPeriods.antiperiod_of_black

data.Note: The forcing period from the parents.
data.Name: TH>Ruliology.CellularAutomata.Rule30RightPeriods.inp_least_period

data.Note: The cascade lemma, in the kit as the input period theorem.
data.Name: TJ>Ruliology.CellularAutomata.Rule30RightPeriods.inp_least_period

data.Note: An accumulated parity of a periodic input is periodic with twice the period.
data.Name: TA>Ruliology.CellularAutomata.Rule30Diagonals.xor_accum_periodic

data.Note: An upper bound on the dyadic exponents: e_j <= (2j + 1)/3.
data.Name: TP>Ruliology.CellularAutomata.Rule30RightPeriods.per_upper

data.Note: e_14 <= 6: the period does not double at every k >= 3 (H2 is falsified in the ledger too).
data.Name: H2>Ruliology.CellularAutomata.Rule30RightPeriods.per_14

data.Note: w_k = D k is eventually periodic with period 2^k, so its least eventual period divides 2^k.
data.Name: TR>Ruliology.CellularAutomata.Rule30Diagonals.D_periodic

data.Note: Uniform bounds on center runs.
data.Name: H13>Ruliology.CellularAutomata.Rule30CenterRuns.black_run_le

data.Note: The left half as the half driven by the center: the frame of B9 and TX.
data.Name: B9>Ruliology.CellularAutomata.Rule30DrivenLeft.cell_eq_L

data.Note: The kit's coupled questions: for every periodic word, no finite halves are coupled to it; together they imply Problem 1.
data.Name: B1>Ruliology.CellularAutomata.Rule30Coupled.problem1_of_CQ

data.Note: The kit's open statement for period 2, in the driven-left-half form: no finite start keeps column -1 black at every even time.
data.Name: B7>Ruliology.CellularAutomata.Rule30PeriodTwo.Q01

data.Note: The same open statement in the zero-boundary form (Q01).
data.Name: B7>Ruliology.CellularAutomata.Rule30ZeroBoundary.Q01

data.Name: B8>Ruliology.CellularAutomata.Rule30Coupled.problem1_of_CQ

data.Name: B5>Ruliology.CellularAutomata.Rule30DrivenLeft.light_cone

data.Note: Any finite prefix of column -1 is realized by some finite start: the free bits of TU.
