data.Proof:
by
  unfold Rule30Prize.Problem1 Rule30Jen.EventuallyPeriodic
  constructor
  · rintro h ⟨T, p, hp, hper⟩
    exact h ⟨p, hp, T, Nat.zero_le _, fun t ht => by simp only [c]; rw [hper t ht]⟩
  · rintro h ⟨p, hp, T, -, hper⟩
    exact h ⟨T, p, hp, fun t ht => bit_inj.mp (hper t ht)⟩
data.Note: Our formal P1 says exactly what the official Problem1 says: c is a 0/1 copy of the kit's center.
data.Name: alignment-P1

data.Proof:
by
  rintro ⟨T, -, h⟩
  exact Rule30Prize.center_not_eventually_period_one ⟨T, fun t ht => bit_inj.mp (h t ht)⟩
data.Note: Period 1 of Problem 1 is the kit theorem, with 0/1 cells.
data.Name: claim-K1

data.Proof:
by
  intro t _
  refine ⟨?_, ?_⟩
  · simp [x, bit, Rule30Jen.cell_left_edge]
  · have h := Rule30Diagonals.R_zero t
    simp only [Rule30Diagonals.R, Nat.cast_zero, Int.sub_zero] at h
    simp [x, bit, h]
data.Note: Both boundary cells are black: the left edge from the kit, the right edge as the zeroth right diagonal.
data.Name: claim-T0

data.Proof:
by
  intro t _ h
  have h' := Rule30MaskedJen.left_of_black t 0 (bit_eq_one.mp h)
  simp only [Int.zero_sub] at h'
  show bit (Rule30Jen.cell (t + 1) 0) = 1 - bit (Rule30Jen.cell t (-1))
  rw [h']
  cases Rule30Jen.cell (t + 1) 0 <;> rfl
data.Note: Left-consistency: after a black center cell the rule forces the next center cell to the complement of x(-1, t).
data.Name: claim-TX

data.Proof:
by
  refine ⟨⟨by simp [x, bit, Rule30Jen.cell], fun i hi => by simp [x, bit, Rule30Jen.cell, hi]⟩, fun t _ i _ => ?_⟩
  show bit (Rule30Jen.cell (t + 1) i) = rule30 (bit (Rule30Jen.cell t (i - 1))) (bit (Rule30Jen.cell t i)) (bit (Rule30Jen.cell t (i + 1)))
  rw [Rule30Jen.cell]
  simp only [rule30, bit_beq_one]
data.Note: The prize setup is the kit's definition of the evolution.
data.Name: claim-D0

data.Proof:
by
  intro p _ t _ hyp
  obtain ⟨h0, h1⟩ := hyp
  have e1 : Rule30Jen.cell (t + 1) 0 = Rule30Jen.rule (Rule30Jen.cell t (-1)) (Rule30Jen.cell t 0) (Rule30Jen.cell t 1) := by
    rw [Rule30Jen.cell]; rfl
  have e2 : Rule30Jen.cell (t + 1 + p) 0 = Rule30Jen.rule (Rule30Jen.cell (t + p) (-1)) (Rule30Jen.cell (t + p) 0) (Rule30Jen.cell (t + p) 1) := by
    rw [show t + 1 + p = (t + p) + 1 by omega, Rule30Jen.cell]; rfl
  simp only [x, c, Rule30Prize.center, bit_inj] at h0 h1 ⊢
  rw [e1, e2] at h1
  revert h0 h1
  generalize Rule30Jen.cell t (-1) = a, Rule30Jen.cell t 0 = b, Rule30Jen.cell t 1 = r,
    Rule30Jen.cell (t + p) (-1) = a', Rule30Jen.cell (t + p) 0 = b', Rule30Jen.cell (t + p) 1 = r'
  cases a <;> cases b <;> cases r <;> cases a' <;> cases b' <;> cases r' <;> simp [Rule30Jen.rule, bit]
data.Note: Column transfer, proved here from the rule at times t and t + p (ours; the kit has the one-step facts left_of_black and left_of_white).
data.Name: claim-TS

data.Proof:
by
  intro k _
  show Function.minimalPeriod shift (y k) ∣ 2 ^ k
  apply Function.IsPeriodicPt.minimalPeriod_dvd
  show shift^[2 ^ k] (y k) = y k
  rw [iterate_shift]
  funext t
  simp only [y, Rule30Diagonals.R_periodic]
data.Note: The least period of y_k divides 2^k, because 2^k is a period (the kit's R_periodic).
data.Name: claim-T004

LeanChecks.Description: What the Lean kernel said about each claim's Lean statement: lean/Rule30Ledger.lean, written from the compiled rulebook and checked by the kit's Check.lean (research/lean/ledger.py). A check counts only while its statement is the claim's current Lean statement.

schema.name: LeanCheckId
schema.Description: <kind>-<claim>.

schema.name: Name
schema.Description: Display alias.

schema.name: Assertion
schema.Description: The claim.

schema.name: Kind
schema.Description: claim or alignment.

schema.name: Theorem
schema.Description: Its name in Rule30Ledger.lean.

schema.name: CheckedStatement
schema.Description: The Lean statement that was checked (for an alignment, our side of the equivalence).

schema.name: Elaborates
schema.Description: 1 when Lean accepted the statement as well-formed.

schema.name: HasProof
schema.Description: 1 when a proof was supplied (otherwise the theorem is a sorry: an open Lean obligation).

schema.name: Ok
schema.Description: 1 when Check.lean passed it: kernel replay, standard axioms only.

schema.name: CurrentStatement
schema.Description: The claim's Lean statement now.

schema.name: IsCurrent
schema.Description: 1 while the statement checked is still the one the build writes.
